rows.description: A child watches another child join a group by asking, "Can I play too?" and repeats the same words the next day at the sandpit, with a smile.

rows.description: A child offers a friend the first turn on the new bicycle in return for playing tag afterwards. Trading what the friend wants for what the child wants opens the play.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, if-then plan, mental simulation

rows.description: A child thinks, "If she says no, I ask Meera instead," and prepares a second choice. The rule keeps a refusal from ending the whole plan.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, mental simulation, negotiation

rows.description: A shy child practises the question "Do you want to play?" with a doll before going out. Saying the words once makes it easier to say them to a real child.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, if-then plan, negotiation

rows.description: A child tells the teacher, "Nobody wants to play with me," and the teacher helps by proposing a group game. The adult gives an entrance the child could not find.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, if-then plan, mental simulation, negotiation

rows.description: A child says, "You have to play my game or I won't be your friend," and the other child walks away. Demanding works less well than offering.

rows.description: A friend says "not now" and the child decides that nobody likes him, and sits alone. One refusal is read as the final word.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, if-then plan, mental simulation, negotiation

rows.description: A child at the slide counts the children ahead and works out, "Three more, then me." Knowing the place in the line makes the waiting easier to bear.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, if-then plan, negotiation, trial and error

rows.description: Another child skips ahead on the swing, so a child says to the teacher, "He didn't wait his turn." The adult is used to settle whose turn it is.

rows.description: A child agrees, "If I get twenty pushes, then I get off," and counts aloud. The rule is agreed in advance, so getting off is less of a fight.
